operations.comment: ; Readability baseline: physical file offsets include the 16-byte iNES header.
; bNN labels identify physical 8 KiB PRG banks, not MMC1 register values.
; Only classified instructions receive executable labels. Numeric control-flow
; destinations that remain are outside classified boundaries or lack a resolved
; switchable-bank context; they do not claim new reachable code.
; work00..work1f are caller-owned scratch reused by unrelated routines.
; Actor fields are bases indexed by the slot offset in X; type bit 7 denotes
; active/on-screen state. Actor world and screen coordinates are distinct.
; Frame header nibbles describe sprite dimensions; OAM records are Y,tile,attr,X.
; actor_saved_y/X and actor_frame_delay are state-dependent union bytes: some
; behaviors retain world coordinates/page there, others use counters or flags.
; strip_even/odd_wrapped_base deliberately rely on zero-page indexed wrap.
; Voice records are 24 bytes; voice_pointer addresses the selected logical voice.
; Current interpretation names mechanical roles; gameplay item/effect identities
; and unvisited branches are unresolved. See ../uncertainties.md.
; Mechanical RAM and hardware symbols. Values preserve original operand widths.
; Consumer-derived ROM address aliases below do not classify their target bytes.
; 24-byte audio voice record offsets; unused fields retain no asserted role.
; Additional shared dialogue/epilogue fields established by the current consumers.
; Round003 static entries assume MMC1 PRG mode three where CHR writes preserve PRG.
; Bank-stack transfers require valid current/shadow agreement, sufficient depth and no
; collision or wrap with CPU frames. A balanced return contract does not prove termination.
; Conditional gates may discard frames; only their documented normal branch resumes locally.
; Actor construction cache and singleton reservations; callers preserve their own union fields.
; CPU aliases for classified data in the operand's effective physical bank view.
; Alternate ADC #4 entry inside the BIT operand at physical 74056..74059.
; CPU aliases for the four-word relocated PPU destination pools (A=0..3).
; Local menu/password/ending unions; their owning routines define index contracts.
; State-specific aliases for the reviewed inventory, projectile and actor paths.
; iNES header: 8 x 16 KiB PRG, 16 x 8 KiB CHR, MMC1 mapper, no trainer. Preserved verbatim.
; CPU addresses for separately identified ROM descriptors; effective bank context is required.
; Event flags and screen-transition fields; these RAM bytes remain state-dependent unions.
; Disable IRQs, reset the MMC1 serial/control state with bit 7, and jump to the fixed-bank reset entry. This is a reset contract, not an ordinary returning call.
; Seven bytes between the terminal reset-bootstrap jump and the bank entry. Repeated $00/$ff patterns support noncode data, but original fill or linker intent is unresolved.
; A selects a little-endian jump-table entry; the destination is staged in dispatch_vector. The three dispatch words are classified below.
; Three little-endian dispatch destinations, indexed by A*2 through dispatch_vector.
; Form a 16-bit index*8 plus record_base in record_cursor. The following entry selects record_base from two tables indexed through scene_tileset.
; Select a record base through the scene-tileset map and pointer table.
; Sixteen scene-tileset selectors; the consumer maps each to one of the record-base words.
; Read byte Y=work3 from record_cursor. Caller owns the pointer and index.
; Six little-endian base addresses. The consumer adds an eight-byte record index; differing base spacing does not establish six complete arrays.
; Record/tile payload selected through TileRecordBases. Consumer, repeated eight-byte patterns and adjacent sprite-code boundary support data; exact internal ownership remains unresolved.
; Continuation of the record/tile payload in physical bank one. This physical split does not assert a separate logical array.
; Skip rendering when actor_count is zero; otherwise the next fragments rotate the first actor to distribute the OAM limit.
; Select the negative four-byte sprite step before rejoining the common OAM traversal.
; Set remaining count, start at the end of OAM, and compare the rotating actor index with actor_count.
; Reset the first actor slot used by the renderer.

; Map logical actor index to a slot; only active nonzero types render. Resolve the frame, emit tiles, and stop at the OAM budget. Rotate the starting actor each pass. The trailing entry resolves a cached frame pointer or looks it up by type and animation flags.
; X is the actor slot; A is type with active bit stripped. Resolve a cached frame or select a type/animation pointer.
; Load the frame-list pointer for the nonnegative animation variant.
; The negative variant selects a second frame table. Low animation bits select a pointer pair, cached in the actor. The next entry splits the frame header into column/row counts and loads screen Y.
; Frame pointer is work00:work01. Split dimension header and seed OAM position/count scratch.
; Return from the completed sprite-render path.
; Write tile, Y, attributes and X into OAM, descending four bytes per sprite. Zero tile and horizontal wrap use the classified clipping continuation.
; Advance past the two remaining frame-record fields.
; Count columns, advance X by eight with wrap detection, then count rows. The row-reset continuation restores cursors and advances sixteen pixels.
; Restore the row cursors, advance the screen Y by sixteen, and stop once the next row reaches the lower clipping boundary.
; Save the OAM cursor. The following entry hides unused sprites with offscreen Y values down to the reserved boundary.
; Hide unused descending OAM slots while preserving the low reserved slots.

; Two-level frame pointers and framed tile payload consumed by the sprite renderer. Header nibbles give dimensions and subsequent bytes supply tile entries; complete frame ownership and pointer domains remain unresolved.
; Sixteen actor-slot offsets used by indexed actor/render traversal.
; Uniform FF bytes ending at the physical bank boundary. No executable or padding-purpose claim.
; Disable IRQs, reset MMC1 serial/control state, and jump to fixed-bank reset. The repeated suffix is data with unresolved fill purpose.
; Seven bytes between the terminal reset-bootstrap jump and the bank entry. Repeated $00/$ff patterns support noncode data, but original fill or linker intent is unresolved.
; A selects an entry through the bank-local pointer table.
; Seventeen little-endian service destinations selected by the scene-bank dispatcher. The banked entry contract determines the effective view; values alone do not prove arbitrary caller indices.
; Prepare a forward scene strip, then select the current stream record unless the alternate orientation path applies. Decode its record byte through the shared strip routine.
; Start the shared strip decoder with Y=0.
; Select the preceding stream record and decode strip mode one. The alternate entry prepares the reverse orientation, clamps a negative strip accumulator to zero, and joins the same record decode.
; Enter the shared attribute walker at the third byte of its record.
; Select the previous scene-stream record and finish the shared strip decoder in mode three.
; Wait for transition state, preserve the current scene, and initialize a vertical scene upload through the fixed-bank service.
; Synchronize rendering, select scene $c0, clear its initial stream position, and derive the scene variant from the high nibble of player Y before common scene setup.

; Restore rendering and scroll after the selected scene service. Pop the scene id saved by the matching entry; wait while PPU sprite-zero hit remains set. Frame/audio return and a matching saved byte are required.
; Scroll down four pixels per update. On wrap, reset the stream and select one of three transition scenes through the twelve-entry scene list.
; Twelve scene-exit keys scanned from index eleven down to zero by the remapping helper.

; When orientation bits $14 are clear, refresh the strip, adjust stream and column cursors at column fourteen, and decode the selected stream byte. Bytes >=$f0 latch the orientation stop bits; smaller bytes enter the strip producer.
; Refresh strip/cursor state before decoding the selected stream byte.
; Mark orientation stop bits for the $f0..$ff stream-byte class.
; Convert the coarse horizontal scroll nibble into tile/attribute column indices; target nametable high byte starts at $20.
; Choose the adjacent wrapped row from camera direction, then derive its nametable byte address and tile/attribute column indices.

; Compute $95df+4*A. The next entry computes record_base+8*A, returning low byte in X and high byte in A. The strip decoder then expands eight packed map cells into paired tile buffers and attribute bits.
; Return record_base+8*A as X low/A high; uses work04 for overflow.
; Initialize scratch for expanding a strip from row Y; eight cells produce sixteen tile pairs.
; Resume the same strip with existing buffer cursor and row index.
; Split palette bits from each metatile index and expand its four tile bytes into the even/odd strip buffers, eight records per strip.
; Derive a quadrant selector from nametable column bits; the branch body supplies Y=1.
; Advance the metatile pointer to the next component.
; Retain the quadrant selector and test the alternate scene orientation.
; Advance past two metatile components.
; Choose an attribute stride for scene orientation, combine adjacent two-bit palette fields and preserve the other nametable quadrants.
; Shift the selected palette quadrant into its packed attribute position.
; Merge the packed palette bits into the attribute buffer, step by the selected stride, and return its $23c0-based PPU destination.

; Noncode bytes retained after inspection of the full local pattern, neighboring ranges and available references. Accepted indexed consumers read within this range, but mixed layout, full selector bounds and ownership remain unresolved.
; For scene IDs below $c0, resolve the stream pointer from a table. Alternate IDs use the classified low-nibble pointer-table paths.
; Mask the stream selector and load its little-endian pointer.
; Select the nonnegative orientation mode after stream selection.
; Load the six-bit stream pointer, mark vertical orientation, and reset horizontal scroll.
; Map an ordinary scene ID through its tileset table; special IDs take another path.
; Use the six-bit record selector to fetch a tile-bank value; enter the shared row handler with thirty rows.
; Select MMC1 resources, metatile and record tables. The following entry decodes paired strip records, expands tile buffers and attributes, then schedules their upload.
; Advance the record index for the shared scene decoder.
; Store the update request and check scene-specific strip adjustments.

; Noncode bytes retained after inspection of the full local pattern, neighboring ranges and available references. Accepted indexed consumers read within this range, but mixed layout, full selector bounds and ownership remain unresolved.
; Read the palette selector for ordinary scene IDs.
; Mask the scene selector and fetch its variant byte.
; Load the palette, then scan ordered scene/variant pairs until matching scene ID; preserve the matching variant.
; Scan paired thresholds until the selected scene matches, then retain the associated variant byte.
; Return from palette/variant selection.
; A indexes three-byte palette records. Load universal color and expand two twelve-color records into four-color groups with the shared color repeated. Request a full palette upload.
; Reload the currently selected palette via the common expansion routine.
; Expand one twelve-byte palette record into four groups of shared universal color plus three colors.
; Use route_id*4 to compare the current junction against the route record.
; Advance through the four-byte route records until the route key matches.
; Install scene_id and stream; the selected half of the route record determines entry-side and scene page state.
; Restore stream/page position from the scene record and request entry motion.
; Read stream length, advance its pointer by one, and initialize actor loading through a banked wrapper.
; Return unless strip work is pending. Clear its latch and select the continuation from A; this is a middle entry of the neighboring strip graph.
; Consume the strip latch and select the value-two continuation.
; Enable PPU increment 32; upload two thirty-byte tile columns, restore scroll between columns, then write eight attribute entries spaced by eight.
; Upload two thirty-two-byte tile rows with PPU increment-one, then copy eight packed attributes from the buffered column.
; Reset the PPU address latch and write the tile destination. The following entry does the same for attributes, then scene setup configures rendering and loads route resources.
; Reset PPU address latch and write the attribute destination.

; Consume the pending scene-scroll override: clear its flag, restore scroll Y from the packed high nibble and write the scroll shadows, then shift the packed low nibble into the high half of the saved position byte and join scene setup.
; Initialize scene/status state, hide projectile slots, enable rendering, and prepare actors. The next entry fills the screen by decoding/uploading sixteen columns with horizontal scroll wrapping.
; Build and upload sixteen columns while scroll wraps by sixteen pixels.
; Build and upload sixteen-pixel strips until the vertical position wraps, then restore rendering and reset column phase.
; Synchronize, upload pending palettes and restore scroll; clear the strip request.

; Choose an exit-record list by scene, compare sorted page keys and direction flags, and install the matching destination stream, scene and entry state. A missing exit can start vertical transition state.
; Initialize twelve inventory slots to value three and compute the available four-unit resource limit from its base count.
; Walk the alternate scene exit list in four-byte records. Match page and direction, install destination fields, or start transition state when the directional edge has no record.

; Disable rendering updates while choosing CHR/control state. Read the scene length, initialize current/next strip indices, and consume its header with a special two-byte offset at initial position zero before the banked scene helper.

; Decode the current stream position and align player Y to the scene row. Move horizontally within the stream or repeatedly request a signed camera step until scroll matches the target. Strip work is serviced while waiting; frame/scroll progress is conditional. Negative orientation seeds the next page and vertical scroll before the common scene continuation.
; Request a positive camera step and service pending strip work until scroll reaches the target.
; Compare the next stream position against stream length before choosing scroll direction.
; Advance camera by one through the selected bank service.
; Advance camera by minus one through the selected bank service.
; Clear the local motion byte; negative orientation prepares the next page.
; Scene variant work is limited to one in four frame-counter phases and requires a nonzero variant.
; Rotate each palette group selected by scene_variant bits, preserve the selector, and request background/sprite uploads for the selected halves.
; Return when scene variant work is not needed.
; Rotate the three non-background colors in the selected four-byte palette group.

; Return when neither scene refresh flag is set, otherwise enter scene setup or rebuild the status display. Hide sprites, clear the nametable, select graphics and upload an inline PPU stream. MMC1 CHR writes preserve PRG only under mode three.

; Two-byte little-endian PPU stream pointer following the calling JSR. E06C/E0DC adjusts the grandparent saved return by two; the enclosing call resumes at JSR+5, with two intact frames and nonwrapping stack indexing required.
; Install a fixed status sprite and restore rendering/control state after the inline upload, then synchronize scroll and frame state.

; Every eighth frame, accept exact held-button values to cycle selector 0..2 and place the OAM cursor. Confirm disables rendering and uploads the inline screen stream; other frames rejoin the polling loop.
; Decrement the screen selector, wrapping through its masked three-state domain.
; Mask selector to two bits and replace value three with zero.
; Disable rendering and begin the inline screen upload.

; Inline little-endian PPU stream pointer. The target at physical 19649..19662 was parsed as 3 finite records. E06C internally calls E0DC: its two intact, nonwrapping frames allow the uploader caller's saved return to advance two and resume at physical 18956, JSR+5. Any outer ending synthetic frame is separate.

E06C internally calls E0DC: its two intact, nonwrapping frames allow the uploader caller's saved return to advance two and resume at physical 18998, JSR+5. Any outer ending synthetic frame is separate.

; Write the edited route nibbles and enter frame-paced input polling.

; Copy entry argument into route_id, clear transition state, select PPU pattern mode, and enter scene setup.
; Upload the junction editor layout with rendering disabled.

E06C internally calls E0DC: its two intact, nonwrapping frames allow the uploader caller's saved return to advance two and resume at physical 19115, JSR+5. Any outer ending synthetic frame is separate.

; Sample junction editing every eight frames.

; Output each route choice as two nibbles with paired padding tiles.
; Sample exact left/right controls or finish on the exit bit.
; Increment the four-way selection.
; Decrement the four-way selection.
; Mask selection to 0..3 and update cursor X.
; Read the selected route, clear its transition and enter scene setup.

E06C internally calls E0DC: its two intact, nonwrapping frames allow the uploader caller's saved return to advance two and resume at physical 19386, JSR+5. Any outer ending synthetic frame is separate.

; Write the edited scene byte at PPU $2210.
; Wait for the sampling gate and a held direction or exit.

; Increment the edited byte modulo 256.
; Decrement the edited byte modulo 256.

; Add $f0 plus incoming carry to the edited byte.
